question: is accent detected by testing meaning, or by scanning a codepoint block?
method: a combining mark counts as a tone mark when its Unicode NAME contains TONE, SVARITA, UDATTA or ANUDATTA, or when it is one of the five Latin GRETIL/VedaWeb tone marks AND its base character is a vowel. U+0301 on a consonant is the letter s-acute and is excluded.

what_the_naive_range_scan_gets_wrong.RV: 10,552 accented by name and base; the naive scan says 7,194, because RV tone marks are U+0331 and U+030D -- neither in the Vedic Extensions block nor in the acute/grave pair -- so the 7,194 it reports are the s-acute characters and the agreement is accidental.
what_the_naive_range_scan_gets_wrong.YV: 1,974 accented by name and base; the naive scan says 780, which is the count of mantras carrying U+1CEA or U+1CEC. Those are ANUSVARA signs, not tone marks. This reproduces the 780 that data/registry/text_versions.yaml was wrongly said to contradict.
what_the_naive_range_scan_gets_wrong.AV: 5,837 accented by name and base against 5,839 by the naive scan: two AV mantras carry no tone mark on any vowel base. The naive scan counts all 5,839 because every AV mantra contains an s-acute.
what_the_naive_range_scan_gets_wrong.SV: 0 by both. The Samavedic verified zero reproduces.
